subject: CIM - error messages and identical lod scores

messages.author: 2ba6a690c64b7d47
messages.subject: CIM - error messages and identical lod scores
parts:
Hello, 

I have been trying to use the CIM function with data from the MSG pipeline (developed by Dr Stern from Janelia). I was advised to use the Haley-Knott regression method but I keep getting this error message:

BCM10.cim3=cim(BCM10.geno, n.marcovar=5, pheno.col="sterile", method="hk", window=10)

Error: BLAS/LAPACK routine 'DGELS ' gave error code -8
In addition: Warning message:
In checkcovar(cross, pheno.col, addcovar, intcovar, perm.strata,  :
  addcovar appears to be over-specified; consider dropping columns.

When I changed the method to "em", I receive an output wherein every marker has an identical lod scores. Has anyone else had this problem? Note that I've also has similar problems when running the scanone function with my data. 

Thanks for your help!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] CIM - error messages and identical lod scores
parts:
If you're using read.cross.mcg, *don't* use calc.genoprob. 

calc.genoprob is for calculating genotype probabilities from genotype data, but you have only genotype probabilities and not called genotypes.

karl

parts: I agree with Karl – take a look at the ancestry-probs* files you import into R/qtl using read.cross.msg and make sure the probabilities and general structure of the files are reasonable. And don't run calc.genoprob

On Tue, Mar 22, 2016 at 11:13 AM Rachelle Kanippayoor <rkanip...@gmail.com> wrote:

Would you be okay if I sent you my data to take a quick look at?

On Mar 22, 2016 11:09 AM, "Karl Broman" <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
It seems like something's wrong with the genotype probabilities you're reading in. hard to tell without looking at the data.

karl

On Mar 22, 2016, at 10:05 AM, Rachelle Kanippayoor <rkanip...@gmail.com> wrote:

I tried that as well and same set of problems - error message when I tried to use haley-knott (error code -12) and identical lod values across all markers.

On Mar 22, 2016 11:04 AM, "Karl Broman" <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
Have you tried using scanone()? I would try that before doing CIM. Does scanone() give you similar problems.

karl

On Mar 22, 2016, at 9:48 AM, Rachelle Kanippayoor <rkanip...@gmail.com> wrote:

So I initially started without using the calc.genoprob (for the reason you provided) then I attempted it with the calc.genoprob. I get the same results regardless. 

On Tuesday, March 22, 2016 at 10:38:23 AM UTC-4, Karl Broman wrote:
If you're using read.cross.mcg, *don't* use calc.genoprob. 

calc.genoprob is for calculating genotype probabilities from genotype data, but you have only genotype probabilities and not called genotypes.

karl

On Mar 22, 2016, at 9:15 AM, Rachelle Kanippayoor <rkanip...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thank you for your response. Yes, I did used the read.cross.msg script and did run the calc.geno function before I ran the cim function. When looking at the genotype probabilities, I tried using the summary function or just typing in the name of my data into R and it only ever produces the following information: # of individuals, # phenotypes, percent phenotyped, chromosome names and # markers. 

On Monday, March 21, 2016 at 8:50:50 PM UTC-4, Andrés wrote:
I assume you used Stern's read.cross.msg and didn't run calc.genoprob after reading in the cross? Have you made sure the genotype probabilities are different between markers and individuals to make sure import worked well?

BCM10.cim3=cim(BCM10.geno, n.marcovar=5, pheno.col="sterile", method="hk", window=10)

In addition: Warning message:

When I changed the method to "em", I receive an output wherein every marker has an identical lod scores. Has anyone else had this problem? Note that I've also has similar problems when running the scanone function with my data. 

Thanks for your help!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] CIM - error messages and identical lod scores
parts:
For an intercross, I'd be wanting at least 100-150 individuals.

For scantwo, there are 9 possible 2-locus genotypes, and 4 of them have frequency 1/16. And you start running into problems when some of those 2-locus genotypes aren't observed.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] CIM - error messages and identical lod scores
parts:
You could try doing a scan for loci that interact with the locus on chr
13, either by including the chr 13 locus as an interactive covariate, or
by using makeqtl() and then addqtl(), the latter using formula= y~Q1*Q2

karl
